messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: GPU reload address wobble — severity P1 :rotating_light:

kai: noticed burst of 502/500s and multiple container restarts in us-west-2-gpu-pool starting ~02:12 UTC. Correlates with model rollout.

ashley: grabbing runtime logs, seeing repeated `CUDA illegal memory access` right after model hot-reloads. stack traces point into KV cache apply path.

ashley: logs:
```
runtime: cuda illegal memory access at 0x7f8a3c1b0f20
serving::kv_cache::apply +0x1a3
pid=1234 container=rw-infer-27
dmesg: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, ... GPU pagefault
```

kai: also seeing OOM kills on a few pods, dmesg shows pagewalk/smmu messages. suspect kernel/driver interaction under concurrent reloads.

infra-eng: recommendation — cordon nodes 12-14 and drain gracefully to avoid noisy restarts. Need to route traffic to fallback capacity.

sre-lead: agreed. Plan: 1) cordon/drain affected nodes, 2) rollback model bundle to v1.9 (pre-reload), 3) disable hot-reload until RCA. Rolling restart serving ds with older kernel module (rtn-1.2.3) if needed.

deploy-bot: rollback triggered by @sre-lead — rolling back model-ref -> v1.9 across us-west-2 shards.

ashley: after rollback, error rate dropped to baseline, but node-12 still showing intermittent flapping. Logs show a late `illegal memory access` during a reload attempt.

kai: mitigation actions: disable model hot-reload, increase eviction threshold (so reloads don't coincide with eviction), kill any hung loader processes.

sre-lead: applying hotpatch: set env RW_DISABLE_HOT_RELOAD=1 in daemonset and restart 3 pods to apply immediately.

commands:
```
kubectl -n rwinf set env ds/serving RW_DISABLE_HOT_RELOAD=1
kubectl -n rwinf rollout restart ds/serving
```

ashley: confirming post-restart: no new `illegal memory access` logs, SMMU counters look normal. GPUs remain online.

customer-success: FYI — CS received a handful of customer reports for elevated 5xxs in west region during the spike (~02:12-02:20 UTC). Preparing external comms.

sre-lead: ETA for full stabilization 15m. Customer comms: outline impact window, mitigation, and next steps (RCA + upstream bug). @customer-success to draft.

customer-success: crafting notice: "Impacted subset of inference requests in US-WEST-2 between 02:12–02:20 UTC. Automatic retries reduced visible errors; no data exfiltration. Follow-up with RCA."

kai: collecting artifacts for RCA: nvcrash logs, core dumps, and serving runtime traces uploaded to s3://redwood-incidents/4360001111/ — saved nv-crash.tar.gz, core_<pid>.gz, and logs.tar.gz.

ashley: initial hypothesis: a kernel driver/pagewalk race triggered by concurrent model reload + eviction path. Will open upstream bug and attach repro with sequential reload+evict.

sre-lead: add a durable alert to catch reload+eviction concurrency (#alert: reload_concurrency) and a metric to track `cuda_illegal_memory_access` occurrences.

kai: handoff: I will be on-call for next 4h to monitor and ensure no recurrence. If stable for 30m we'll downgrade to P2 and file postmortem.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATED: severity -> mitigated. Actions: cordon+drain, rollback to model v1.9, disable hot-reload, collect artifacts, draft comms. Next steps: RCA, upstream bug report, hotpatch plan.

ashley: filing internal ticket with repro steps and attaching s3 artifacts. Tagging research/infra for possible kernel-level followup.

kai: ack. monitoring grafana dashboard and the `illegal_mem_access` alert. will escalate if errors reappear.

sre-lead: handing off final watch to @kai. I’m pausing active rotation. Good job team — keep incident notes short for postmortem.
